Overview – 2014 Adimab Collaboration Agreement (2014 Adimab Agreement)
paragraphs: We are a clinical-stage biotechnology company developing therapies for neurodegenerative diseases, with a focus on areas of high unmet medical need. Our work is informed by advances in disease biology, including the roles of misfolded or deficient proteins, lysosomal dysfunction, and immune and neuronal pathway disruption.

Our objective is to develop product candidates that address disease through targeted mechanisms, such as removing pathogenic proteins, replacing deficient proteins, and restoring normal cellular function. We are advancing a portfolio of programs focused on genetically validated targets, supported by our expertise in drug development, protein engineering, and antibody discovery.

A key component of our strategy is the development and application of our Alector Brain Carrier (ABC) platform, a proprietary blood-brain barrier (BBB) delivery technology designed to improve central nervous system exposure across multiple therapeutic modalities. We continue to refine and expand this platform to enable effective brain delivery at clinically practical doses of antibodies, enzymes, and siRNA therapeutics. In parallel, we are investing in biomarkers and biomarker assays to guide patient selection, demonstrate target and pathway engagement, and assess biological impact in the clinic, with the goal of improving development efficiency and the likelihood of technical success.

Our portfolio includes nivisnebart (formerly AL101/GSK4527226), an investigational progranulin (PGRN)-elevating antibody that has completed enrollment in a placebo-controlled, double-blinded Phase 2 study in early Alzheimer's disease (AD) under our July 2021 Collaboration and License Agreement (GSK Agreement) with Glaxo Wellcome UK Limited, a subsidiary of GlaxoSmithKline plc (GSK).

In addition, our wholly owned programs include lead candidates in preclinical development for a brain-penetrant anti-amyloid beta antibody for Alzheimer's disease and a brain-penetrant GCase enzyme replacement therapy for Parkinson's disease (PD) and Lewy body dementia (LBD). We are also advancing brain-penetrant siRNA programs targeting tau for Alzheimer's disease, α-synuclein for Parkinson's disease, and NLRP3, with potential applications across multiple neurodegenerative conditions.

Nivisnebart is an investigational human recombinant monoclonal antibody designed to elevate PGRN levels in the brain. Its pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic properties may be suitable for treating prevalent neurodegenerative diseases. We and GSK are co-developing nivisnebart for the potential treatment of early AD, and it may also be evaluated for other indications, including PD. Loss of function (LOF) mutations in the GRN gene, which moderately reduce PGRN levels, have been shown to increase the risk of developing AD and PD. Conversely, increased PGRN levels have been demonstrated to be protective for those diseases in animal models. Given the strong link between GRN LOF mutations and neurodegeneration, elevating PGRN levels may provide a potential therapeutic approach that offers broad neuroprotection in both AD and PD.

In April 2025, enrollment was completed in PROGRESS-AD, a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, 76-week Phase 2 global clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of nivisnebart in slowing disease progression in early AD. Trial completion is expected in 2026. An independent interim futility analysis is planned for the first half of 2026. In August 2025, the first patient from PROGRESS-AD was enrolled and dosed in the optional open-label extension (OLE) study, and enrollment in the OLE is ongoing. Under the current terms of the GSK Agreement, we are responsible for funding and sharing GSK's and our development costs up to $140.5 million for the conduct of the initial Phase 2 trial of nivisnebart in early AD.

In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1 study in 88 healthy volunteers who received either single or multiple doses of nivisnebart administered intravenously or subcutaneously, nivisnebart was generally well tolerated and elevated PGRN levels in cerebrospinal fluid.

We have expanded and continued to advance our preclinical and research pipeline by leveraging our expertise in neuroscience and applying our proprietary blood-brain barrier technology platform, Alector Brain Carrier (ABC). Built on the core design principles of versatility, differentiated binding, and translatability to a distinct region of the transferrin receptor (TfR), ABC is intended to support the targeted delivery of therapeutics to the brain and to optimize safety and efficacy at lower doses. With a wide range of TfR binding affinities and binding kinetics, and the ability to target a distinct epitope of TfR, the platform can be aligned with the requirements of diverse therapeutic cargos, including antibodies, enzymes, proteins, and siRNA. The platform's TfR binding domain is further adaptable to diverse engineered formats, enabling broad applicability to our product candidates. By leveraging these proprietary features, we aim to achieve efficient transport of our product candidates across the BBB with the goal of balancing brain uptake, potency, and safety. Our strategic approach positions us to develop therapeutic candidates for a range of neurodegenerative diseases.

As part of our efforts to advance our programs through development and execute on our strategic plan, we may seek to partner with other biopharmaceutical companies. To date we have had three licensing, co-commercialization, or co-development agreements for certain programs in our pipeline, one of which is currently active.

AL137 is our proprietary anti-amyloid beta (Aβ) antibody paired with our proprietary ABC in preclinical development for the potential treatment of AD. It is designed to remove brain Aβ plaques, with the potential for minimal treatment related incidence and/or severity of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) and the potential to enable subcutaneous delivery. AL137 features a high-affinity, fully human antibody that selectively binds PyroGlu3, a validated epitope on the toxic form of Aβ found in plaques, a fully active effector function that enables maximal recruitment of myeloid cells to remove plaques, and Alector's proprietary ABC with tuned affinity, binding kinetics, and binding epitope designed to facilitate brain penetration and plaque removal while minimizing hematologic adverse effects. In preclinical studies to date, AL137 has demonstrated robust brain penetration in non-human primates, and an AL137 surrogate has demonstrated amyloid beta 42 reduction in murine studies.

We have selected AL137 as a lead candidate, with AL037 as our back-up candidate, and we are targeting submission of an Investigational New Drug (IND) application in the fourth quarter of 2026 or the first quarter of 2027, based on the timing of GMP clinical supply production.

AL050 is a GCase enzyme replacement therapy paired with our proprietary ABC technology in preclinical development for the potential treatment of Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia in patients having GBA1 gene mutations that lead to reduced GCase activity. AL050 features an engineered GCase with improved activity and stability, a silenced effector function to maximize safety, and Alector's ABC with a TfR epitope and affinity designed to enhance delivery across the BBB. An AL050 surrogate was shown in vivo to rescue GCase activity in GBA1 deficient mice. This mechanism aims to reduce cellular dysfunction and slow disease progression. In preclinical studies to date, AL050 doubled GCase activity in both rodents and non-human primates and reduced toxic substrate accumulation in a rodent GBA disease model with no apparent hematologic findings or other adverse effects, supporting its potential as a therapy for Parkinson's disease and Lewy body dementia associated with GBA LOF mutations.
We have selected AL050 as a lead candidate, and we are targeting submission of an IND application in 2027.

We may not be successful in our efforts to obtain approval for additional or expanded indications for any product candidates that receive approval for a given indication.
We may encounter substantial delays in our clinical trials or may not be able to conduct or complete our clinical trials on the timelines we expect, if at all.

paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should carefully consider the risks described below, as well as the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our financial statements and the related notes and the section titled "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," and in our other public filings, in evaluating our business. The occurrence of any of the events or developments described below could harm our business, financial condition, results of operations, and growth prospects. In such an event, the market price of our common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your investment. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently deem immaterial also may impair our business operations and the market price of our common stock.

Our business is subject to numerous risks and uncertainties that you should consider before investing in our company, as more fully described below. The principal factors and uncertainties that make investing in our company risky include, among others:

• We are in various stages of drug development and have a limited operating history and no products approved for commercial sale, which may make it difficult to evaluate our current business and predict our future success and viability.
• We have incurred significant net losses in each year since our inception and anticipate that we will continue to incur net losses for the foreseeable future.
• Drug development is a highly uncertain undertaking and involves a substantial degree of risk.

• We will need to obtain substantial additional financing to complete the development and any commercialization of our product candidates, and a failure to obtain this necessary capital when needed on acceptable terms, or at all, could force us to delay, limit, reduce, or terminate our commercialization efforts, product development, or other operations.

Our operations have been financed primarily through our collaboration with GSK, our previous collaboration with AbbVie, entered into in October 2017 and terminated in February 2025, the issuance and sale of convertible preferred stock and of common stock upon the completion of our initial public offering (IPO), and follow-on equity financings.

To date, we have not had any products approved for sale and have not generated any product or royalty revenue from product sales. Further, we do not expect to generate revenue from product sales until such time, if ever, that we are able to successfully complete the development and obtain marketing approval for one of our product candidates. We will continue to require additional capital to develop our product candidates, advance our research and preclinical programs, and fund operations for the foreseeable future. We have incurred net losses in each year since inception, and we expect to continue to incur net losses for the foreseeable future. Our ability to generate product revenue will depend on the successful development and eventual commercialization of one or more of our product candidates. Our net losses were $142.9 million and $119.0 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, respectively. As of December 31, 2025, we had an accumulated deficit of $972.1 million. Substantially all of our net losses have resulted from costs incurred in connection with our research and development programs and from general and administrative costs associated with our operations. We expect our expenses will increase substantially in connection with our ongoing activities, as we:
• advance product candidates through preclinical studies and clinical trials; • pursue regulatory approval of product candidates;
• discover, validate, and develop additional product candidates;
• require the manufacture of drug supply for our research, preclinical studies and clinical trials; and
• obtain, maintain, and protect our intellectual property portfolio.

On March 7, 2025, we committed to a plan to reduce our workforce by approximately 13% to better align our resources with our strategic priorities including advancing our preclinical and research pipeline. We initiated such reduction in force impacting approximately 25 employees across the organization. On October 21, 2025, we initiated a reduce in force that impacted approximately 47% our workforce in order to align resources with the Company's strategic priorities following the results of the Phase 3 INFRONT-3 clinical trial evaluating the safety and efficacy of latozinemab in individuals with frontotemporal dementia due to a progranulin gene mutation (FTD-GRN). As of December 31, 2025, we had cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities of $256.0 million, which we anticipate provides runway at least through 2027.

概要 – 2014年Adimab合作契約（2014年Adimab契約）
paragraphs: 本公司為一間臨牀階段的生物科技公司，專注於開發治療神經退化疾病的療法，特別著重於高醫療需求未被滿足的領域。我們的工作受到疾病生物學進展的啟發，包括錯誤摺疊或缺乏的蛋白質、溶酶體功能障礙，以及免疫與神經路徑的破壞等角色。
我們的目標是開發產品候選藥物，透過針對性的機制來治療疾病，例如去除病原性蛋白質、取代缺乏的蛋白質，以及恢復正常的細胞功能。我們正在推進一組專注於遺傳學驗證目標的計畫，這些計畫由我們在藥物開發、蛋白質工程及單株抗體發現方面的專業知識所支撐。

我們策略的一個關鍵零組件是開發與應用我們的 Alector Brain Carrier (ABC) 平台，這是一項專有的血腦屏障 (BBB) 運輸技術，設計用以提升多種治療模式在中樞神經系統的暴露程度。我們持續優化並擴展此平台，以實現在臨牀上實際劑量下對抗體、酵素及 siRNA 療法的有效腦部遞送。同時，我們也在投資生物標記物與生物標記物試驗，以指導病患篩選、顯示目標與路徑的參與，並評估臨牀上的生物影響，目標為提升開發效率與技術成功的機率。

我們的產品組合包括 nivisnebart（原為 AL101/GSK4527226），這是一款正在研發中的 progranulin（PGRN）提升單株抗體，已完成在早期阿爾茨海默病（AD）的安慰劑對照、雙盲 Phase 2 研究的入組，根據我們與 Glaxo Wellcome UK Limited（為 GlaxoSmithKline plc（GSK）的子公司）於 2021 年 7 月簽訂的合作與授權協議（GSK 協議）。

此外，我們的 wholly owned 計畫包括在臨牀前開發階段的腦穿透性抗 amyloid beta 抗體用於阿爾茨海默病，以及腦穿透性 GCase 酵素替代療法用於帕金森病（PD）與路易體失智症（LBD）。我們也在推進針對 tau 的腦穿透性 siRNA 計畫用於阿爾茨海默病、針對 α-synuclein 的腦穿透性 siRNA 計畫用於帕金森病，以及針對 NLRP3 的腦穿透性 siRNA 計畫，這些計畫可能適用於多種神經退化疾病。

nivisnebart 是一款正在研發中的人類重組單株抗體，設計用以提升腦內 PGRN 水準。其藥動學與藥效學特性可能適合用來治療常見的神經退化疾病。我們與 GSK 共同開發 nivisnebart，用於潛在治療早期 AD，並可能評估用於其他適應症，包括 PD。GRN 基因的功能喪失（LOF）突變，會中度降低 PGRN 水準，已被證明會增加罹患 AD 與 PD 的風險。相反地，在動物模型中已顯示增加 PGRN 水準對這些疾病具有保護作用。根據 GRN LOF 突變與神經退化的強烈關聯，提升 PGRN 水準可能提供一種潛在的治療方法，為 AD 與 PD 提供廣泛的神經保護。

2025 年 4 月，PROGRESS-AD 研究完成入組，這是一項隨機、雙盲、安慰劑對照、76 週的 Phase 2 全球臨牀試驗，評估 nivisnebart 在減緩早期 AD 疾病進展的安全性與有效性。試驗預計於 2026 年完成。計畫於 2026 年上半年進行獨立的中期無效性分析。2025 年 8 月，PROGRESS-AD 的第一個病患已入組並接受開放標籤延長研究（OLE）的治療，且 OLE 的入組仍在進行中。根據目前 GSK 協議的條款，我們負責為 nivisnebart 在早期 AD 的初始 Phase 2 試驗的執行，支付並與 GSK 共享開發成本，總計高達 140.5 百萬美元。
在一項隨機、雙盲、安慰劑對照的 Phase 1 研究中，88 名健康志願者接受單次或多次 nivisnebart 靜脈注射或皮下注射，結果顯示 nivisnebart 通常耐受良好，並能提升腦脊液中的 PGRN 水準。

我們已擴展並持續推動我們的臨牀前及研究藥物開發管道，透過運用我們在神經科學領域的專業知識，並應用我們專有的血腦屏障（BBB）科技平台，Alector Brain Carrier（ABC）。此平台基於靈活、差異化結合及可轉譯至轉鐵蛋白受體（TfR）特定區域的設計原則，旨在支持藥物針對大腦的遞送，並在較低劑量下優化安全性與療效。透過廣泛的TfR結合親和力與結合動力，以及能針對TfR特定表位的特性，此平台可與多種治療載體（包括單株抗體、酵素、蛋白質及siRNA）的開發需求對應。此平台的TfR結合域進一步可適應多種工程化格式，使其能廣泛應用於我們的產品候選藥物。透過運用這些專有特性，我們旨在實現我們產品候選藥物在BBB的高效遞送，目標在於平衡大腦吸收、藥效與安全性。我們的戰略方法使我們能開發針對多種神經退化疾病的治療候選藥物。
作為我們推動藥物開發計畫並執行戰略計畫的一部分，我們可能尋求與其他生物製藥公司合作。截至目前為止，我們已與三家生物製藥公司簽訂了授權、共同商業化或共同開發協議，其中有一項協議目前仍為有效。

AL137為我們專有的抗β-胺基酸（Aβ）單株抗體，搭配我們專有的ABC平台，目前處於臨牀前開發階段，用於潛在治療阿爾茨海默症（AD）。其設計為去除大腦中的Aβ斑塊，並具有潛在的最小治療相關症狀與/或嚴重度的胺基酸影像異常（ARIA），並具備皮下給藥的潛力。AL137具備高親和力、全人類單株抗體，選擇性結合PyroGlu3，這是已驗證的Aβ毒性形式在斑塊中之表位，具備完整的效應功能，能最大化的招募髓細胞去除斑塊，並搭配Alector專有的ABC平台，其親和力、結合動力與結合表位經過調整，設計用以促進大腦穿透與斑塊去除，同時最小化血液學不良反應。根據目前的臨牀前研究，AL137在非人類靈長類動物中已顯示出強大的大腦穿透能力，且AL137的替代物在小鼠研究中已顯示出β-胺基酸42的減少。
我們已選定AL137為主要候選藥物，AL037為備選候選藥物，並預計在2026年第四季或2027年第一季提交新藥臨牀試驗申請（IND）。

AL050為一種GCase酵素替代療法，搭配我們專有的ABC技術，目前處於臨牀前開發階段，用於潛在治療帕金森氏症與路易體失智症，針對具有GBA1基因變異導致GCase活性降低的患者。AL050具備改良的GCase活性與穩定性，並具備靜音效應功能以最大化安全性，並搭配Alector的ABC技術，其TfR表位與親和力設計用以增強穿越BBB的遞送。AL050的替代物在體內實驗中已顯示可恢復GBA1缺陷小鼠的GCase活性。此機制旨在減少細胞功能異常並延緩疾病進展。根據目前的臨牀前研究，AL050在小鼠與非人類靈長類動物中將GCase活性提高一倍，並在小鼠GBA疾病模型中減少有毒底物的累積，且未觀察到明顯的血液學發現或其他不良反應，支持其作為治療帕金森氏症與路易體失智症相關GBA LOF變異的潛力。
我們已選定AL050為主要候選藥物，並預計在2027年提交IND申請。

paragraphs: 您應閱讀下列對我們財務狀況及營運成果之討論與分析，並與本年度10-K表報表所附之合併財務報表及相關附註一併參考。本討論包含風險與不確定性之向前看陳述，包括在「向前看陳述特別說明」節中所描述之風險。我們實際之結果及部分事件之時程可能與下列討論有重大差異。導致此差異之因素包括，但不僅限於，下列所列及在本報告其他部分「風險因素」節中所列之因素。
我們是一家臨牀階段生物科技公司，專注於開發用以治療神經退化性疾病之療法，特別著重於高醫療需求未被滿足之領域。我們之工作受到疾病生物學進展之啟發，包括錯誤摺疊或缺乏之蛋白質、溶酶體功能異常，以及免疫與神經路徑受損之角色。
我們之目標為開發可透過針對性機制來治療疾病之產品候選藥物，例如去除病原性蛋白質、取代缺乏之蛋白質，以及恢復正常細胞功能。我們正在推進一組專注於遺傳學驗證目標之計畫，此計畫受到我們在藥物開發、蛋白質工程及單株抗體發現方面之經驗所支持。
我們策略之關鍵零組件為開發與應用我們之Alector Brain Carrier (ABC)平台，這是一項專利之血液腦屏障(BBB)遞送技術，設計用以提升多種治療模式之中央神經系統暴露。我們持續改善並擴展此平台，以實現於臨牀實用劑量下對抗體、酵素及siRNA治療藥物之有效腦部遞送。同時，我們正在投資於生物標記物及生物標記物測試，以指導病患篩選，並顯示目標及路徑
參與並評估臨牀中的生物影響，目標為提升開發效率與技術成功的機率。

我們的產品組合包含 nivisnebart（ formerly AL101/GSK4527226），一種正在進行臨牀試驗的 PGRN 增加型單株抗體，已於 2021 年 7 月合作與授權協議（GSK 協議）下，完成 enrolment 的安慰劑控制、雙盲 Phase 2 試驗，針對早期阿爾茨海默病（AD）患者，該協議為與 Glaxo Wellcome UK Limited（GlaxoSmithKline plc（GSK）之子公司）所簽訂。
此外，我們的 wholly owned 研發計畫包含針對阿爾茨海默病（AD）的腦穿透性抗 amyloid beta 抗體及針對帕金森病（PD）的腦穿透性 GCase 酶替代療法的 lead 候選藥物。我們同時也在推進針對阿爾茨海默病的 tau、帕金森病的 α-synuclein 以及 NLRP3 的腦穿透性 siRNA 計畫，這些計畫可能應用於多種神經退化性疾病。
我們的營運資金主要來自與 GSK 的合作、我們先前與 AbbVie 的合作（於 2017 年 10 月簽訂，於 2025 年 2 月終止）、發行及銷售可轉換優先股與普通股（於我們首次公開發行股票（IPO）完成後）、以及後續的 equity 融資。

截至目前為止，本公司尚未有任何產品獲得銷售批准，亦未從產品銷售或版稅收入中產生任何收入。此外，本公司預期在成功完成某項產品候選藥物的開發並取得市場批准之前，不會產生來自產品銷售的收入。本公司將持續需要額外資金以開發產品候選藥物、推進研究與臨牀前計畫，並支應可預見未來的營運資金需求。本公司自設立以來每個年度均產生淨虧損，且預期在可預見的未來仍將持續產生淨虧損。本公司產生產品收入的能力將取決於產品候選藥物的開發成功及最終商業化。本公司淨虧損為 142.9 百萬美元及 119.0 百萬美元，分別為 2025 年 12 月 31 日及 2024 年 12 月 31 日所終結年度的數字。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，本公司累積虧損為 972.1 百萬美元。本公司淨虧損幾乎全部來自與研究與開發計畫相關的費用，以及與營運相關的總務及行政費用。本公司預期因持續進行活動，費用將大幅增加，因為我們：
• 將產品候選藥物推進至臨牀前研究及臨牀試驗； • 追求產品候選藥物的監管審批；
• 發現、驗證並開發更多產品候選藥物；
• 要求製造藥品供應以用於我們的研究、臨牀前研究及臨牀試驗；以及
• 取得、維持並保護我們的智慧財產權組合。

於 2025 年 3 月 7 日，我們承諾了一項計畫，以減少約 13% 的員工數量，以更好地將資源與我們的戰略優先事項對齊，包括推進我們的臨牀前研究與研究管道。我們已啟動此項減員措施，影響約 25 名員工。於 2025 年 10 月 21 日，我們啟動了另一項減員措施，影響約 47% 的員工，以根據公司戰略優先事項調整資源，此舉是基於 Phase 3 INFRONT-3 臨牀試驗的結果，該試驗評估了 latozinemab 在因 progranulin 基因突變所致前額葉失智症 (FTD-GRN) 患者中的安全性與有效性。截至 2025 年 12 月 31 日，我們持有現金、現金等價物及市場可交易證券共 256.0 百萬美元，我們預期此資金可支持至少至 2027 年。

headings: 與我們業務、財務狀況及資金需求相關的風險
自我們成立以來，我們每年均產生顯著的淨虧損，並預期在可預見的未來，我們仍將持續產生淨虧損。
藥物開發是一項高度不確定的任務，並涉及相當程度的風險。
我們的貸款協議要求我們遵守特定的營運約束條款，並對我們的營運及財務彈性設有限制。
與我們產品候選藥物的發現、開發及商業化相關的風險
我們可能無法成功達成努力以取得任何已獲批准產品候選藥物針對其他或擴展適應症的批准。
我們可能在臨牀試驗中遭遇重大延誤，或可能無法按照我們預期的時間表進行或完成臨牀試驗，甚至可能無法完成。

paragraphs: 投資本公司普通股涉及高度風險。您應仔細考慮下列所描述的風險，以及本年度報告表 10-K 中的其他資訊，包括財務報表及相關附註，以及標題為「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」的章節，以及本公司其他公開申報文件，以評估本公司業務。上述任何事件或發展發生，可能會對本公司業務、財務狀況、營運成果與成長前景造成損害。在這種情況下，本公司普通股的市場價格可能會下跌，您可能會損失全部或部分投資。此外，尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前尚未為本公司所知或本公司認為不重要，也可能影響本公司業務運作與普通股的市場價格。
本公司業務面臨許多風險與不確定性，您在投資本公司前應加以考慮，詳情請參見下列更詳細說明。使投資本公司成為風險的主要因素與不確定性包括，但不限於：
• 我們處於不同階段的藥物開發中，且具有有限的營運歷史與無經核准上市銷售的產品，這可能會使評估本公司目前業務與預測未來成功與可持續性變得困難。
• 自本公司成立以來，我們每年均產生顯著的淨虧損，且預期未來可預見的期間內，我們仍將持續產生淨虧損。
• 藥物開發是一項高度不確定的任務，並涉及相當程度的風險。
• 我們將需要取得大量額外資金以完成產品候選藥物的開發與任何商業化，若無法在需要時以可接受的條件或完全無法取得此必要資金，可能會迫使我們延遲、限制、減少或終止商業化努力、產品開發或其他業務運作。
